page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture (Neoverse-V2) running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU allocation provides one thread per core with no simultaneous multithreading. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the baseline network bandwidth is 8 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8gd.4xlarge demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong uncached read and write memory bandwidths of 296.76 GB/sec and 130.55 GB/sec respectively. Multi-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15957.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 198.16 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, with PassMark database benchmarks scoring in the strong tier and Redis SET operations reaching 35.39 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU tasks and static web serving throughput align with average tiers.

Tradeoffs are visible in large language model inference workloads. While prompt processing for a small 135M model is average at 1044.44 tokens per second, text generation for the same model is poor at 41.2 tokens per second, and text generation for a 70B model drops to a poor 2.41 tokens per second. This indicates the server is not optimized for heavy LLM text generation. Given the high memory-to-core ratio, strong database performance, and local NVMe SSD storage, the r8gd.4xlarge is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, caching layers, and data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is an ARM64 memory-optimized server featuring 16 dedicated physical cores on the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, a 950 GB local NVMe SSD, and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It exhibits top-tier memory performance and strong multi-core capabilities, particularly in database operations and large-block memory bandwidth, while single-core CPU tasks align with average tiers. However, it shows poor performance in large language model text generation tasks, making it less suitable for generative AI workloads. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, caching systems, and data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and high-speed local NVMe storage.
